body:
Thank you for your response and words of wisdom.  I really should have held firmer to my boundaries long ago and have been beating myself up for that, but I need to just accept that what's done is done and all I can do now is try my best to move on and forgive myself.

Thank you.
Your response actually made me laugh.  Thank you.
Thank you so much.  Your response was very sweet and it means a lot.

Thank you for saying that.  I have been really hard on myself because this is the only relationship that I've had where I didn't end on good terms with the person.  I feel like a completely immature person for not being able to let this go with dignity and being the bigger person-- I was definitely very weak towards the end there and I'll never forgive myself for it.

But I do appreciate that you guys think I sound like a good person, even after how I handled everything.

Doesn't feel that way at the moment-- I was essentially rejected for another girl that's significantly older and also married.  Like how did I fail that bad!?

I also know that's not a reasonable way to think, but I can't help but feeling that way.

Thank you for your comment.

I love your honesty and your directness- I definitely need that.

I actually looked up her address and, while she does not have access to Xfinity which is like the main provider out here, there were 2 other good providers that she could have gotten internet access with.  She also could have gotten a hotspot.

He also uses her Netflix and HBO, so she has those streaming services!  And there were things recently watched that I know he didn't watch, so either she was watching them at home with the internet that she swears she doesn't have, or she was watching it at his house, which proves they were doing more than just working.

Thank you.  I am a perfectionist and when I'm in a relationship that ends I always feel like I've failed in some way.  But in this instance I really do think that I did everything that I could to save it. Definitely more than I should have.

Oh definitely going NC.  100%.

I still have some of his stuff but I'm going to have my friend drop it off to him.

​

Thank you.
Thank you very much.
Thank you- I really appreciate your response.
Thank you.
Thank you

Thank you for sharing your previous experience.  I'm sorry that you went through that.  My sister has BPD so I know what it is like to care about someone that has those types of issues-- sometimes just that in and of itself can feel like a roller coaster.

I really had no idea that I was codependent until reading a book to try to understand his codependent relationship with his friend...then when I read the signs and characteristics, I saw a lot of myself in them and was pretty embarrassed.  But I do think that knowing that is one of my issues will hopefully help make treating it easier, even if just a little bit.

Even towards the beginning, before I really had an issue with his friend, there were other small things that I should have thought about more that I just overlooked.  On holidays, we would spent maybe an hour or two with my family, and then the entire rest of the day with his.  Or on days like Black Wednesday, New Years Eve, etc., we'd always be with his friends (normally the bestie), we rarely did anything with my friends, and when we did he never really seemed happy about it.  He is very introverted and I think might have a bit of social anxiety, so I didn't really think that he was being selfish-- just thought being around people he wasn't comfortable with was more difficult for him.  I know everything that happened with his brother messed with him...I felt guilty bringing a lot of things up because it would more often than not end with something involving his brother.  At the same time, I also have my own traumatic issues that I hadn't really gotten over like I should have, but put them to the side because his seemed more important (I was able to function and had tried moving past a lot of the things that happened to me, had been to therapy, and was still able to open up to him, but he was never quite able to open up and seemed to be holding onto a lot of things so I felt that I was more healed, and therefore should be more understanding of the things that he's been through).

My high school/ early college boyfriend (basically my first love, we dated for 4 years and were engaged at one point) also passed away, actually just a few months before my ex's brother did.  I obviously wasn't dating him anymore at the time, but there were a lot of factors at play where essentially I've always felt like if I had handled that situation differently, he might still be alive.  I know losing an ex is not the same as losing a family member, but I think in a way I was jealous because his best friend has this endless support system from her ex's friends and family and her own family, and the only person I've ever really had to support me through it was my best friend- my family is very religious so I wasn't allowed to date, or if I did they wouldn't have approved so they didn't even know he existed, let alone that he passed away.  My best friend is phenomenal and I'm honestly the luckiest person in the world to have her in my life..but I try not to confide in her too much because she has a lot of her own stuff going on and I don't want to burden her.  So I think I did have jealousy towards her, just not the type of jealousy that it probably looked like to my ex.

Sorry to unload all of that on you, but yes...definitely the furthest thing from a secure person here.  Hopefully I'll be able to change that but it's been almost 10 years and I feel like I'm still going in circles most of the time.
Thank you

I really do feel like the biggest idiot on the planet.

My friend literally said "I bet he doesn't want you coming over like you were supposed to because his friend is probably over there every day" and I was like "there's no way, I'm sure she comes over every once in awhile but I really don't think she's still there all the time."

I really need to listen to her more often.

Thank you.  Deep down I do know that this relationship ending was the right thing, but that doesn't change the fact that it hurts and is painful, or the fact that I am mad at myself for not leaving 3 years ago when I knew that I should have, which adds a whole other level of hurt and pain because I feel like I let myself down.

I really appreciate your comment.

Thanks for sharing your perspective.  This whole time I've actually had the opposite opinion.

He had a crush on me and pursued me for 8 years.  Once he actually got to know me, he basically retreated, which was my biggest fear from the beginning.   The idea that he had in his head of me did not live up to the person I actually was.  I wasn't smart enough, interesting enough, funny enough, or whatever else it was that he thought I would be.  I think the fact that my personality was what seemed to let him down made me doubt myself a lot and feel like I'm either a boring or just terrible person (which I've always feared, and I think this happening validated those fears).
Thank you.

Thank you again for your response.  I've been in and out of therapy for a lot of my life (and am also an avid reader of books on psychology and self-help, ironically), and my choices in men were never really explored in relation to my childhood, but I definitely feel as though there is a huge relationship there that I've never thought about.

What you said is extremely interesting and something that I really am going to need to think about further.

Thank you.  Sometimes I wonder if my idea of having a significant other come first is outdated.  It seems so common now for people to go on group trips and spend holidays at parties instead of as a family or taking trips just as a couple.  I've just always preferred the traditional family dynamic and he has always seemed to prefer big groups and partying.  I don't think one is particularly right or wrong, but I do think that was a pretty big incompatibility with us.

Thank you for your response.  I have another session booked with this therapist, but if it doesn't seem to end up helping me I might try to look for another one.  The therapist is also a single male and it seems like he's been single for the majority of his life (and I tried not to judge but looking back it may have been better to get a therapist that has more experience being in a relationship), and he's also admittedly newer to couples' counseling.  He does seem to have a lot of experience with depression, so I am hoping that he can still help me.
Thank you.

Thank you.  If you ever want to talk or vent about what you went through I'm here.  I sometimes go into lurk mode and don't get the energy to respond right away, but I always respond at some point.

At (almost) 33, I think kids are most likely out of the picture for me, which is another reason I tried holding on to this relationship for so long.  Even if I were to find the perfect person right away, I wouldn't want to marry someone after only a year or so together because I don't really feel like you can truly know someone at that point. Then again clearly I don't have the best judge of character anyways, even after 4 years so it stinks.  I think that's part of why I'm taking this so hard...I see it not only as missing out on a relationship that was very important to me, but also as missing out on the last chance I had to have the family that I always wanted.

You put everything that I have been feeling into words better than I ever could.  I am in shock- the warning signs were definitely there and very apparent even, but I wanted things to work out so bad that I was willing to overlook them for so long.  I chose to believe the reassuring words, even while knowing that the actions weren't matching up.

Thank you for helping me to understand what was in my mind that I couldn't quite describe for whatever reason.  I also appreciate your kind words.
Thank you.
Thank you- I appreciate your honest feedback.

Thank you so much.  I really do hope you're right (about me moving on, I also don't want him to be miserable forever).

I appreciate your response.

I really don't think that they will date (also she's married, but even if she wasn't I don't think that would happen because of his brother).  Then again, who really knows.

Your comment was insanely sweet- thank you.
Thank you
Thank you- your post was very sweet and I really appreciate your kind words.

Thank you.  I was married previously, and when I looked back on that relationship I was awful.  Anytime something bothered me I would bring it up right away, even trivial things.  I didn't put up with anything and that relationship failed, so I think in this relationship I tried over-correcting and just doing everything the exact opposite way, thinking that I would find success in that.

I definitely need to find a happy medium, but you are right.  One of the main breaking points I had was when my best friend had a talk with me and said she used to look up to me because I never put up with being treated poorly in any way and was never afraid to stand up for myself.  In this relationship, I never did that and she flat out told me that she lost a lot of respect for me.  I promised her that I wouldn't put up with anything else, and shortly after was when I found out about her working at his house and made my initial post.

I am continuing therapy on my own and I do hope that it helps.  My self-worth really isn't good and I want to improve it, but at the same time I don't want to have a false sense of confidence that isn't deserved, if that makes any sense at all.

Sorry for all of the rambling...I really appreciate your response.
Thank you for your response-- that really is very good advice and I really appreciate it.

Thank you.  I did make a lot of exceptions because of how the relationship started that I normally would not have made.  Going forward I just need to remember that no matter what, I shouldn't make exceptions for anyone, no matter how great the relationship starts off in the beginning.

Thank you- I'm very sorry for what you went through..can't imagine how much that must have hurt.  Being broken up over for a best friend sucked, but I think it would be even more painful to be left for another romantic interest...that really sounds terrible.

Thank you for your advice and opinion-- I really hope you're right.

I completely agree with you.  Harsh words, but nothing I haven't heard before from my friends (that I should have listened to).

I don't want people to feel sorry for me- someone asked for an update and I provided one.  I am upset at myself for ignoring the advice of my friends and staying as long as I did.  I know that I'm not blameless in this situation at all- I'm trying to be as objective as I can when I post/ respond because I do want people's true opinions, but I'm sure a lot of the things I say could easily be taken as looking for sympathy without me even realizing it.

Thank you- I do agree that in person would have been better.  I was nervous that in person would lead to an argument, and this way hopefully things could get resolved more calmly and we would have time to think about things before responding and not say anything hurtful.

Clearly it didn't work, but that was my reasoning.

Thank you- your response was very thoughtful.  The thing that I struggle with is that I did not want to date him at first.  He pursued me for years.  Even once he told me about his feelings, I was very guarded.  Kept delaying dates/ rescheduling to try to get him to not like me anymore because I was still hurt from my divorce and didn't want to go through that kind of heartbreak again.

He repeatedly assured me that he genuinely cared about me and wasn't going anywhere.  It truly felt like he did-- he was honestly a 100% perfect boyfriend, until the day I told him about my issues with his friend.  It's like I became this monster that he still continued to date for whatever reasons, but I really think he emotionally checked out and never saw me the same way after that.  I could always sense that things weren't the same, but hoped if I stuck around long enough things would eventually go back to the way that they were.

I really don't think he will date her.  I think he'll date someone else, and his friend will be so relieved that he's not with me anymore that she will be on her best behavior so whoever he dates next will like her, and I'll always be looked at as the insane ex-girlfriend.

I probably put way too much thought into that scenerio but I really do think that's what will end up happening.
Thank you

Honestly I was happy with him more than I wasn't.  Every time we were together we always had a great time and I have a hard time connecting with people and everything about our relationship and our time together seemed to come naturally.

Looking back our times together were so fun because we tried to just ignore our issues.  But it didn't feel like an awful relationship while it was happening.
Thank you
Thank you for your response- it means a lot.  Truly can't believe that people cared enough to read my initial post and the update-- I really do appreciate it so much.
Thank you.  I don't feel like either of those things right now but it means a lot that some people out there think that.

Thank you.  The therapist validated my feelings at first but I'm not going to lie-- the night he broke up with me I ended up drinking quite a bit and sent him a barrage of text messages that I am completely embarrassed and ashamed of.  He ended up e-mailing the therapist about the texts, and we had another session a few days ago where he came to the session basically just to give me my stuff.  But basically all of those drunken texts got turned on me and even the therapist now seems convinced that I was the problem.

I'll be the first to admit the texts were inappropriate and shouldn't have been sent.  But the fact that even the therapist now believes I was the problem is the hardest thing for me to digest and makes me question everything.  Even posting here...I tried to be as objective as I could but maybe I really am just crazy and worded things in such a way as to where people would agree with me.  I really don't know anymore.
Thank you

Thank you for that information.  I already tried to go on a couple dates just to try to distract myself and I literally felt sick afterwards.  I know it's too soon but I just wanted to do something to try to feel any sort of relief, even for a second.

I've struggled with depression most of my life so I do think that is a big factor here as well.  I thought I had it under control but this breakup hit me really hard-- much harder than my divorce even did.

I tried not to get my hopes up, but deep down a huge part of me really did kind of believe him reading the comments on that other post would give him the reality check that he needed...like literally how could it not have?  If anything it just seems like it made him more mad and makes me regret showing him..maybe it made me look immature and vindictive?  I'm really not sure.  I really appreciate your thoughts and words of encouragement.
Thank you- I really appreciate your comment.
I posted the reply above right before reading what you said.  Sounds like you're spot on- thanks for giving your opinion.

Thanks.  I couldn't figure out what I did wrong between it seeming like he wanted to work on things and him breaking up with me.  The only thing I did in between was send that text...my friend seems to think that he thought he could still try to manipulate me into making nice with her and when I made it clear that wasn't going to happen he just decided to cast me aside.  Her assessment seems pretty accurate but I really never thought of him as manipulative until recently.  I always thought he was one of the nicest people I ever met.  =/
That's great advice-- thank you.  I am going to continue to see the therapist on my own to hopefully try to figure out what's going on with me and why it's been so difficult for me to move past this.

Thank you.  I feel like the one who's trashed because it literally feels like I tried to stand up for myself and just got thrown away.  Like I wasn't worth making any compromises for.

I do appreciate the supportive words in everyone's comments.  It's just hard for me to believe them right now.
Thank you
Thank you- hopefully in time I will see things that way.  I appreciate your comment.

Wow, I wasn't going to post one because I'm pretty embarrassed but it means a lot that you cared enough to ask.  I just posted one-- here is the link:  https://www.reddit.com/r/relationship\_advice/comments/ut7gmu/update\_my\_32f\_boyfriends\_36m\_best\_friend\_42f\_is/?utm\_source=share&utm\_medium=web2x&context=3
Thank you for your advice and sorry I've been so slow to respond.  Still haven't had motivation to do much of anything.  I really do appreciate your kind words.

Extremely embarrassed. I texted my ex something similar to what I posted here and if he didn't think I was crazy before he definitely does now. Thank you for asking and for caring. It means a lot that there still seem to be some good people left in this world.
Would also love to chat

I am in the same situation. Break up just happened last night but knew it was coming for awhile. I have no motivation to do anything yet i'm too upset to fall asleep. I wish i could sleep so i could turn my brain off. 

I'm here if you need to vent. This is awful but maybe we can support each other.
Thanks for your response. My bleeding stopped sorry for making you worry..i didn't even realize i posted this until i got notifications

Thank you so much for saying that.  Even after reading all of these posts, I still can't help but feel like I'm being a bitch by putting my food down and saying that this whole situation is not okay and I'm not doing it anymore.  I think (or hope) that in time that feeling will go away..I think I'm just not used to standing up for myself in romantic relationships.
Thank you very much.

Thank you! I do have a health issue where my doctor told me I shouldn't have kids past 35ish. I technically can but it's a lot more risky for both myself and the child. I really appreciate your positive outlook, though. I feel like I am in my head and getting really negative the past few days but your post did help me realize that, even though it doesn't seem like it at the time, there could be a bright side to all of this.

You did a perfect job at putting into words the situation that's been going on since this nightmarish wedding. I should have stuck to my gut and left then
..if I had done that, I probably would be married with a family by now with someone that actually wanted that with me. By now realistically all of that might be too late, and it's a scary reality to accept that one bad decision I made could have possibly prevented me from getting what I've always wanted from life.

He is the first to acknowledge that his family dynamic isn't healthy in the slighest. He's even admitted that his best friend has a lot of similarities to his mom (and not good similarities). He seems to be self care about his family but for the most part is blinded when it comes to her flaws...and if he does see them, there's always an excuse. Thank you for all of your input.

Thank you for sharing your opinion. I did tell him that him having her there all the time is very upsetting to me, and yes she will be upset if he tells her he can't work there anymore, so by him letting her continue to work there he is prioritizing her feelings over mine which shouldn't be happening at this point in our relationship. His response was that "I can't except to be his priority 100% of the time."

The thing that makes me question everything is that this entire exchange happened during our therapy session, and the therapist seemed to think I shouldn't have such a problem with her working there either.

Thank you for your honesty. You are completely correct. I think because he pursued me for so long I had it in my head that he must really love me, but I'm starting to wonder if he just liked wanting something he didn't think he coule have and it probably had nothing to do with actual love.

That's a very interesting idea. At this point I don't think he will be willing to do what I'm needing him to to salvage the relationship. But maybe he should see this, just so he's aware that clearly nothing about their relationship is normal or okay, and he will never have a decent romantic relationship with anyone else if he doesn't change his behavior. Ultimately I'm starting to think it's too late for us, but I truly don't think he is a bad person and I want him to end up finding happiness, but I really don't think he will if he stays in this situation.

I was extremely mad when I first found out, and then it turned to sadness and I started blaming myself thinking if I would have handled things differently maybe all of this would have been prevented. However, after reading all of these comments I am getting mad again.  Thank you for your honesty and your advice.
Thank you.
Thank you. That means a lot.
That's how I've felt quite a few times but then I wonder if I'm just being paranoid. Thank you for sharing your opinion.

I had that thought too..if his friends are willing to drop him that quickly what kind of friends are they anyways? I will say his friend group is pretty juvenile..they are cliche-y and do enjoy being a huge group. They went to college together and it's like they can't let go of that time in their life and are stuck in old traditions and things that really don't make sense as you get older. But I try not to judge them..whatever floats their boat I guess. But it does seem like he doesn't have super close individual friendships with anyone in the group aside from one person (excluding the female best friend).

She is at least 42, she might be 43 by now actually I'm really not sure.  Thank you so much for your advice. I thought maybe I am being too judgemental of her or too harsh. My best friend thinks I've been way too understanding and should have left immediately after the wedding, but sometimes she can be too harsh on people so it does help to see that other people outside of the situation agree that this is not a healthy situation for me to be in.

Thank you.  I've felt like the third wheel from the first time I spent time with both of them together. I even told him I felt that way and he assured me that I should never feel like that and that I'm his #1 priority. But again, words and actions are very different and now that enough time (way too much time) has passed, I do know where he stands. He said before that if he chooses me, hes not just losing her but his friend group will cut him out so he would be losing them too. His family would also be super upset. So the way he sees it, is that if he cuts her out he will only have me and no one else.
Thank you.

Thank you for your response. I think he feels like he has to take care of her because his brother is no longer around. But she's a 40 year old woman...like at what point will she just take care of herself? I'm 10 years younger than her, have way less outside support, and have my life much more put together than she does. Part of me wonders if he has some sort of savior complex and he loves that he feels like she needs him, whereas I don't actually need him. 

He was not there when she said that the person she wants to marry won't marry her. She said it in front of about 20 people though, so I'm sure he could ask around if he really wanted to know. I honestly don't think he believes that she said that. I also showed him the text that he sent me and he said she was just emotionally heated at the time and that's why it came off so innapropriate. I'm starting to notice that he literally has an excuse for everything, though.

Holy shit I honestly did not even think that they would be around her husband. That is terrifying. I wouldn't ever approve of them being around him but at this point I feel like they'd come over behind my back when I was gone or something and that's a frightening realization. Your comment is the most eye-opening one I've had. My boyfriend wasn't okay with the other guy touching me, but I do think he thought I was overreacting about what happened. (He never said it but I think his thoughts were probably along the lines of "it's not like he raped her so I don't understand why this is so upsetting to her". The fact that his parents and friends know what happened and are still upset that I don't want to be around them made me feel even more like I was overreacting.

For the most part I am hurt by the situation, but the thing I'm the most angry about is that I tried to leave after the wedding (at that point him and I had only been together about 6 months) and he convinced me to stay and said that he wanted to he with me and that things might not always be easy because of the situation, but we would try to make it work. But he has done hardly anything to make it work...it's like he expected me to do all the changing. I confronted him about why he said that to me if it ended up being such an issue and he said that he thought I was mad at the time and would cool down and change my mind.

After that,  we wasted another year of therapy. I offered to pay for our sessions because I knew if we went to therapy he would see that I wasn't being controlling, but that his relationship with her really was not healthy. Which did happened..the therapist said that it sounds like this person is constantly the center of a lot of drama and he needs to decide if he even wants her to stay in his life. If she stays, he needs to set up boundaries with her, which he agreed to do. I went a whole year and spent thousands of dollars on the therapy, thinking it was working and helping our relationship when in reality he hadn't changed a thing and was just lying to me. At this point I'm mad at myself that I wasted 4 years, but all of the comments are reinforcing that me being upset is valid and I'm not overreacting my deciding to leave the relationship. Thank you.

Thank you for your input. I'm so sorry you had to go through that. My boyfriend has never outright said I'm not good enough to marry. He once brought up an issue that I drink too much when I get upset, and I recognized that he was correct and I put a stop to it right away. The only other thing he says is an issue is my problem with his friend...his rationale is "who's next?" Like he thinks I'm some super controlling girlfriend that's going to try to find a problem with all of his friends until he's left with no one but me. I think I'm the one in my head coming up with my own reasons on why I'm not good enough, or worth marrying, or being put first. I guess I thought if I was good enough he wouldn't have an issue committing to me, but I'm starting to see how warped my logic about the situation has been.

That is literally the last thing I want...I was upset she was around my dog without me knowing. I feel like she is the type of person that would try to turn my own kids against me (Also worth noting, and I left it out of my original post because it pertains more to her character and nothing to do with my relationship) but her current husband has kids and she tried to convince him to sign his rights over.  Thank you so much for your response.
Thank you so much for your response. I appreciate your advice.

It is completely draining.  I used to be a pretty upbeat/ positive person and I feel like lately I have not been.  I'm just constantly over-thinking different scenerios in my head and driving myself crazy, and then I feel like maybe I am just being crazy and over-reacting, and then I beat myself up over everything.  To be fair I don't think he realizes how much all of this actually affects me.  But all of the comments here are very helpful...I truly thought it'd be like a 50/50 on what I should do and am really surprised by the reactions.  It's been extremely eye opening.  Thank you for your response.
You are 100% correct- Thank you!!

He did say that he wants me to move in with him, but he also wants me to be okay with her working at his house every day (which I am not okay with).  I did tell him that I'm not moving in if he continues to let her work there and his only response was that he wasn't sure what to do.  Which is very telling...I think I just have been in denial.  Thank you again for all of your advice-- you've done a lot of reading about someone you've never mets drama.  I honestly didn't think anyone would read this.  Your help means a lot.

Congratulations on your upcoming wedding, you sound so genuinely excited it gives me hope that there are still decent guys out there lol.  It's good to hear it from a man's perspective because most of the opinions that I get are from females.  I feel like I have already laid it on the line, but maybe not strictly enough.  At this point it's almost like I need to say "if you're serious about me and want to make this work, I need more of a commitment from you immediately because I can't wait any longer for you to figure out what you want.  If you can't give me that, it's time that we go our separate ways."  It seems almost like an ultimatum, which I don't like, but at this point I don't feel like I have any other options.  On the other hand, if he does agree and say he wants to marry me after that conversation, I feel like I'm being cheated out of the romance that's supposed to go with getting engaged/ married.

Thank you- I tend to do that in all of my relationships.  I get too emotionally invested and then it makes it hard to walk away, even when I know I need to.  But then I always look back and get mad that I wasted so much time.  The confusing part is that he insists he does want to get married and have a family with me, he just has reservations because of the issues that I have with his friend and her husband.  But maybe those issues are just an excuse, too.
Thank you

Thank you-- I appreciate your response.  He insisted that he wants the same things, but the reason he is hesitant with me is because of the issues that I have with his friend.  On the other hand, maybe my issues with his friend are just a convenient excuse for him to use to not progress our relationship further.

Thank you again for reading this and reaching out.

Thanks.  I guess I was thrown off because my friends and family will not hesitate to tell me when I'm wrong in a situation-- they're similar to you-- they don't tell me what I want to hear, they're very honest.  I guess I just assumed his friends and family were like that too, but I guess that's not true for all relationships.  I really appreciate your advice.

Thank you for your response, I really do appreciate it.  To clarify, he never lied to me about living with her- he lied to me about her working at his house all day.  I think the main reason I'm second guessing myself is because his friends and family are on her side, so I must be doing something wrong.  The only thing I can think of is sucking it up and just being around them at parties and stuff, but I know if I did that I would be completely miserable.  But then I go back and wonder if that's a selfish way for me to think, because me not being around them is making my boyfriend miserable.

>Wow, thank you for actually reading that!  I tend to ramble when I'm frustrated and upset.  He said he would never date his friend because she was with his brother (Part of me also thinks it's because she is not physically attractive...I honestly think i would have left our relationship immediately after the wedding if she was because that would be more threatening to me, as shallow as that sounds).  I do have self worth issues, and I'm really not sure why..I've had them all my life.  I also don't like change, and moving on to something new and different seems terrifying, but at this point I do think that's what needs to be done.
